back: A business owned and controlled by one person, who keeps all the profit and has unlimited liability.
A business owned by two or more people (commonly up to twenty) who share capital, control and profits.
Owners are personally responsible for all the business's debts; personal possessions can be taken to pay them.
Written agreement setting out capital, profit-sharing ratio, salaries, duties and how disputes are settled.
If partners have no agreement, profits and losses are shared equally.
A partner who provides capital, takes no part in management and has liability limited to that capital.
They have no separate legal identity, so the business may end when an owner dies, retires or goes bankrupt.

front: Sharing profit after a partner's salary
back: Deduct the salary from profit first, then share the remainder in the agreed ratio; add the salary back to that partner's share.
Weigh the owner's wish for control and all the profit against the extra capital, skills and shared workload a partner brings.
